title: Microsoft Teams: third-party synthetic audio and video detection in meetings
summary: The briefing passes: its policy controls, provider prerequisites and licensing statements are supported by Microsoft's documentation. It accurately distinguishes the roadmap's Rolling out status from Learn's public and private preview experiences, and reports the revised Targeted Release window.

claims.claim: Teams is adding integration with certified third-party synthetic audio and video detection solutions for meetings.
claims.quote: Organizations can enhance meeting security with synthetic audio and video detection solutions provided by certified third-party providers.

claims.claim: The third-party provider performs synthetic media detection.
claims.quote: Important: Synthetic media detection is performed by the third-party provider.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Teams supplies the platform integration and in-meeting experiences and controls for provider detection signals.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams provides the platform integration and experiences for surfacing and acting on detection signals from supported providers.

claims.claim: The Graph beta reportSyntheticMedia action lets a certified detection bot admitted to the call report a participant it identifies as synthetic.
claims.quote: This action is intended for certified third-party audio and video synthetic media detection bots admitted to the meeting call. The detection bot calls this action to flag a participant whose stream it identifies as AI-generated or synthetic media.

claims.claim: The Graph detection result is propagated to all participants through roster updates.
claims.quote: The detection result is propagated to all participants via roster updates.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Microsoft asks administrators to select a provider, deploy its app through Teams admin center Manage apps, grant permissions and configure meeting policies.
claims.quote: administrators should evaluate and select a supported detection provider, deploy the provider app through Manage apps in the Teams admin center, grant required permissions, and configure applicable Teams meeting policies.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Third-party detection requires administrator configuration of a provider rather than starting automatically in an unconfigured tenant.
claims.quote: As an admin, you choose a detection provider that meets your organization's needs and turn on detection through a Teams meeting policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Certified third-party providers may analyse meeting audio and video signals.
claims.quote: Certified third-party providers may analyze meeting audio/video signals for synthetic media detection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft asks administrators to review provider terms, data handling and compliance documentation before enabling detection.
claims.quote: Review provider terms, data handling, and compliance documentation before enabling.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's listing declares the Calls.AccessMedia.All application permission for real-time meeting audio and video analysis.
claims.quote: Calls.AccessMedia.All | application | The app is a meeting-recording bot, so it needs Graph to join Teams meetings and access the real-time audio and video media in order to run authenticity and deepfake analysis.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's attestation is the developer's self-assessment and Microsoft does not guarantee its accuracy.
claims.quote: The information on this page is based on a self-assessment report provided by the app developer on the security, compliance, and data handling practices followed by this app. Microsoft makes no guarantees regarding the accuracy of the information.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents is a Defender advanced hunting table for Teams synthetic media detections.
claims.quote: The SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents table in the advanced hunting schema contains details about synthetic media (deepfake) detection events in Microsoft Teams in your organization.

claims.claim: The hunting table is populated from Microsoft Defender for Office 365 records.
claims.quote: This advanced hunting table is populated by records from Microsoft Defender for Office 365.

claims.claim: The table holds data only when an approved detection engine is used.
claims.quote: This table contains data only if you're using an approved detection engine: Microsoft or a third-party engine.

claims.claim: Synthetic media detection hunting is a Microsoft 365 E5 or Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 capability.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5 and Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 extend Teams protection with a set of extra capabilities designed to disrupt the attack chain:

claims.claim: Detection hunting records identify flagged users and the source meeting.
claims.quote: DetectedUserDisplayName | string | Display name of the user flagged as using synthetic media; SourceContextName | string | Name of the source (for example, the meeting, file, or email name)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Prerequisites; Governance controls
claims.claim: A third-party bot can report detections only if the meeting tenant administrator grants Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All as an application permission.
claims.quote: Third-party bots can invoke this action only when the meeting tenant administrator grants the app the Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All application permission.

claims.claim: Saving the meeting policy does not validate that the App ID identifies a supported provider or that the bot can join.
claims.quote: Successfully saving the policy does not guarantee that the App ID identifies a supported provider or that the detection bot can join meetings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: An incorrect or unsupported App ID can prevent the detection bot from joining eligible meetings.
claims.quote: An incorrect or unsupported App ID can prevent the detection bot from joining eligible meetings.

claims.claim: In private preview the organizer can Remove a flagged participant from the alert or roster.
claims.quote: From the alert or the roster, the organizer can: Remove the flagged participant from the meeting.

claims.claim: In private preview the organizer can select Mark as not a concern from the alert or roster after verifying the participant.
claims.quote: Mark as not a concern to dismiss the alert when the organizer has verified the participant.

claims.claim: Teams does not automatically remove flagged participants.
claims.quote: Teams doesn't remove participants automatically. The organizer decides what action to take.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's publisher-attested listing says hosts can rescan a participant.
claims.quote: Hosts can rescan a participant or end the meeting if manipulation is detected.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's publisher-attested listing says hosts can end the meeting if manipulation is detected.
claims.quote: Hosts can rescan a participant or end the meeting if manipulation is detected.

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.claim: Users receive the global meeting policy unless a custom policy is created and assigned.
claims.quote: Users get the global policy unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting protection > Synthetic audio and video detection provider > Turn on synthetic audio and video protection reaches the detection control.
claims.quote: Under Meeting protection, select a provider from the Synthetic audio and video detection provider dropdown list. The Turn on synthetic audio and video protection setting appears and is on by default.

claims.where: controls[0].api; What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy-name> -SyntheticMediaDetection Enabled -SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId <supported-provider-app-id> configures a policy's third-party detection provider.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "SyntheticDetectionPolicy" -SyntheticMediaDetection Enabled -SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId "<supported-provider-app-id>"

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block reaches the app allow/block control.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <value> changes the app's tenant state using a Boolean value.
claims.quote: -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant. Type: Boolean

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetection defaults to Enabled, which permits detection when a configured provider is available.
claims.quote: Enabled: Permits synthetic media detection when a configured detection provider is available. This is the default value. To configure a third-party provider, also set the SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId parameter.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope: Users and policies; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetection controls meetings organised by users assigned the policy, and Disabled turns detection off regardless of the configured provider.
claims.quote: In Example 5, the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet disables synthetic audio/video detection for meetings organized by users assigned this policy, regardless of the configured detection provider.

claims.claim: Disabling detection leaves the configured App ID unchanged.
claims.quote: The SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId value is unchanged.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId defaults to the zero GUID, which does not select a third-party provider.
claims.quote: The default value, the zero GUID (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000), selects no provider when Microsoft Detection is unavailable, or Microsoft Detection when it is available. It does not select a third-party provider.

claims.claim: Selecting a provider from the dropdown causes the Turn on synthetic audio and video protection setting to appear.
claims.quote: Under Meeting protection, select a provider from the Synthetic audio and video detection provider dropdown list. The Turn on synthetic audio and video protection setting appears and is on by default.

claims.claim: The feature page specifies Teams Administrator or higher to manage the app and meeting policies.
claims.quote: You have the Teams Administrator role (or higher) to manage the app and meeting policies.

claims.claim: App availability, required consent, provider-side activation and meeting policy configuration are distinct prerequisites.
claims.quote: If the provider appears but detection doesn't start, verify consent, provider-side activation, the organizer's effective policy, and the meeting option.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes an example using -IsBlocked $true as unblocking the app.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: Allowing or blocking the provider app governs the app itself rather than changing the meeting policy detection setting.
claims.quote: An admin allows the provider's Teams app and grants admin consent to the permissions it needs. The admin turns on synthetic audio and video detection in a Teams meeting policy, selects one provider, and assigns the policy to organizers.

claims.claim: The App ID parameter documentation refers to Microsoft Detection when it is available.
claims.quote: selects no provider when Microsoft Detection is unavailable, or Microsoft Detection when it is available.

claims.claim: A detection is the provider's assessment rather than proof of manipulation.
claims.quote: Detection (verdict) | The provider's assessment that a specific participant's audio, video, or both appear to be synthetic or manipulated.

claims.claim: Synthetic voices and faces can be used to impersonate people in live meetings where money moves or access is granted.
claims.quote: attackers can convincingly impersonate executives, colleagues, job candidates, or vendors during live meetings. These attacks typically target the moments where money moves or access is granted, such as payment approvals, remote hiring interviews, and live social engineering.
